Consult Summary:
- The patient reports a several-day history of widespread itchy, dry skin consistent with an eczema flare (chest, hands, and inside elbows, with elbows being the worst area). No fever or systemic symptoms; no weeping. Recurrent eczema with prior emollient use and OTC steroids; inadequate response to past treatments. Plan includes adding an oral antihistamine (fexofenadine) and a stronger topical corticosteroid (Betnovate) while continuing emollients, with prescription sent to Boots and follow-up in two weeks or sooner if worse.

Problem List:

Issue 1:
- Widespread eczema flare with pruritus and dryness
  - Onset: past few days; progression: worsening over the past few days
  - Affected areas: chest, hands, inside of elbows (elbows worst)
  - Symptoms: very itchy; dry; no weeping; cracks noted on some areas; no thickened/darkened skin
  - Past/med history: history of eczema; previously used Diprobase (emollient) and Dermal; OTC hydrocortisone previously; cetirizine attempted with no relief
  - Medications related: Diprobase, Dermal (emollients); OTC hydrocortisone; cetirizine tried; plan to start Betnovate topical and fexofenadine
  - Exam/physical: no formal exam findings documented
  - Differential/Plan: eczema flare considered; plan to treat with Betnovate topical (topical corticosteroid) and oral antihistamine; continue emollients; monitor response

  - Medications: blue inhaler (prn); no regular controller noted
  - Exam/physical: none documented
  - Plan: not specifically altered in this visit; ongoing asthma management as per patient report

Issue 3:
- Medication history related to dermatitis/asthma management
  - Past/current meds: Diprobase (emollient), Dermal (emollient), OTC hydrocortisone; cetirizine tried; plan includes fexofenadine (new antihistamine) and Betnovate topical
  - Allergies: none reported
